questions.stem: What is Entity Recognition, commonly known as NER, used for?
options: Identifying and extracting meaningful entities from unstructured text
questions.explanation: Named Entity Recognition identifies and extracts entities — people, organisations, locations, dates, amounts and domain terms — from unstructured text.

questions.stem: By what other names is Entity Recognition also known?
questions.explanation: It is also referred to as entity identification or entity extraction.

questions.stem: In the data science lifecycle, at which stage is Entity Recognition typically applied?
options: After the final report is written
questions.explanation: Before modelling or analytics, unstructured text must be transformed into structured features — that is where NER is applied.

questions.stem: In the sentence "Ali visited Kuala Lumpur on 5 January 2026 to meet PETRONAS executives", what type of entity is PETRONAS?
questions.explanation: The chapter's example identifies Ali as a Person, Kuala Lumpur as a Location, 5 January 2026 as a Date and PETRONAS as an Organization.

questions.stem: Which extraction approach compares text against known dictionaries or master data lists?
questions.explanation: Exact-match processors compare text against known dictionaries or master data lists; hybrids combine statistical learning with rules.

questions.stem: What is the first step in building any data model?
questions.explanation: The first step in any data model is entity identification; Entity Recognition helps dig entities out of unstructured datasets.

questions.stem: How does Entity Recognition support data governance?
options: By enriching metadata and improving data lineage tracking back to unstructured origins
By replacing the need for a data catalogue
By limiting who can log in
questions.explanation: Consistently identified entities can be tagged and catalogued, improving lineage tracking even to unstructured origins.

questions.stem: Which is an example of a more advanced Entity Recognition capability?
options: Distinguishing between two different people who share the same name
Counting the words in a document
questions.explanation: Advanced capabilities include distinguishing identical entities, extracting relationships between entities and linking entities to master reference systems.

questions.stem: In the school example "I met Mr. Ahmad on Monday to discuss the Math exam", what would "Math" be identified as?
questions.explanation: Mr. Ahmad is a Teacher (Person), Monday a Date, and Math a Subject — which then become columns in a simple school table.

questions.stem: From a data modeller's point of view, what is Entity Recognition?
options: A bridge between unstructured chaos and structured clarity
A way to avoid conceptual modelling
A technique only for social media data
questions.explanation: Entity Recognition acts as a bridge between unstructured chaos and structured clarity, surfacing real-world entities embedded in narrative data.
